notes: Implementation-planning skill: turns scope into a short, specific phase/task table with verifiable done conditions, explicit dependencies, and optional per-stage assignments; saves docs/streams/[feature]-[YYYYMMDD]/plan/PLAN.md. Evaluate that positives produce an actionable plan; the end-to-end delivery boundary should not fire, since delivery is a sequence of separately gated stages rather than one skill.

evals.prompt: Write an implementation plan for the search feature with a task breakdown and verification criteria.
evals.expected_output: Produces a one-screen plan (docs/streams/search-[YYYYMMDD]/plan/PLAN.md): phase/task table naming specific files/endpoints, input/output per task, explicit dependencies, status values, and concrete done conditions. Tasks are small, focused, verifiable, and ordered — no verbose or generic 'implement feature' entries.

evals.prompt: Create a multi-agent execution plan for building the dashboard, with parallel agent assignments.
evals.expected_output: Produces a plan with the parallel-execution extension: phase/task rows assigned to the owning stage skills (implement-feature, unit-test Mode A, integration-test Mode A), noting that implement-feature --parallel fans out to cbr:developer workers, and marking which phases are independent vs sequenced by dependency, plus done conditions. Saved to docs/streams/dashboard-[YYYYMMDD]/plan/PLAN.md.

evals.prompt: Take the login feature from requirements all the way through design, implementation, and tests end to end.
evals.expected_output: Should not fire, because this asks for end-to-end feature delivery across all SDLC stages, not just writing the implementation plan artifact. Correct response is to name the stage sequence (analyze-requirement, then design-screen/design-function, then implement-feature, then unit-test/integration-test) and start at the first one — each stage gates on user approval, so nothing runs the whole chain.
